subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw models status --probe --all — per-model health check across all configured models

question: Should OpenClaw add `models status --probe --all` as the canonical all-configured-model health probe, or should this behavior be folded into fallback-chain testing or staged model migration instead?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but this creates a new live CLI diagnostic mode with cost, rate-limit, JSON-contract, and overlap implications that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Approve Status Probe All
options.body: Add `--all` to `models status --probe` with explicit cost/redaction semantics and coverage for primary, fallback, image, and scoped agent model refs.

options.title: Fold Into Fallback Testing
options.body: Let https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/6599 own fallback-chain validation and avoid making status probe a broad model execution surface.

options.title: Defer To Migration UX
options.body: Treat model health checks as one step in staged model migration and keep this issue open until that broader workflow is scoped.

recommendation.title: Approve Status Probe All
recommendation.body: Add `--all` to `models status --probe` with explicit cost/redaction semantics and coverage for primary, fallback, image, and scoped agent model refs.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest combined history in the model status/probe path and prior product-scoping reviews for this cluster.
